NONE: › the main artery (= thick tube carrying blood from the heart) that takes blood to the other parts of the body
› a dangerous swelling of the wall of the aorta (= the body's largest artery)

example: Less than half the people with ruptured aortic aneurysms survive.
主動脈瘤破裂的病患只有不到一半的存活率。

NONE: › a physical problem present from birth in which a part of the aorta (= the body's largest artery) is too narrow

example: With aortic coarctation, pulses in the arms are stronger than those in the legs.
主動脈縮窄情況發生時，手臂脈搏比腿部的有力。

NONE: › an operation to treat an aortic aneurysm (= a dangerous swelling of the wall of the aorta) at a point where the aorta leaves the heart
› a narrowing of the heart valve that supplies the aorta (= the body's largest artery), reducing the blood flow to the aorta

example: He had been suffering from aortic stenosis and died of heart failure in his sleep.
他主動脈瓣狹窄，在睡夢中死於心臟衰竭。

NONE: › a condition in which the valve between the heart and the aorta (= the body's largest artery) does not work properly

example: Untreated aortic valve disease can lead to heart failure.
主動脈瓣疾病如不及時治療可能引起心臟衰竭。
